written.myAnswer: A scalar quantity has magnitude only. A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction.

Distance equals the magnitude of displacement when an object moves in a straight line in one direction without reversing. If the path is curved or the object changes direction, distance is greater than the magnitude of displacement.

Distance is the length of the actual path travelled and is a scalar quantity. Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance from the initial to the final position, with direction, and is a vector quantity.
